scenes.text: Bean definitions are recipes. Managed instances are the actual objects.
scenes.phonemes: bˈiːn dˌɛfɪnˈɪʃənz ɑːɹ ɹˈɛsᵻpˌiːz. mˈænɪdʒd ˈɪnstənsᵻz ɑːɹ ðɪ ˈæktʃuːəl ˈɑːbdʒɛkts.

scenes.text: Register configuration, then refresh. Spring reads the definitions and creates our singleton beans.
scenes.phonemes: ɹˈɛdʒɪstɚ kənfˌɪɡjɚɹˈeɪʃən, ðˈɛn ɹᵻfɹˈɛʃ. spɹˈɪŋ ɹˈiːdz ðə dˌɛfɪnˈɪʃənz ænd kɹiːˈeɪts ˌaʊɚ sˈɪŋɡəltən bˈiːnz.

scenes.text: Calling get bean returns the service, already wired to its repository.
scenes.phonemes: kˈɔːlɪŋ ɡɛt bˈiːn ɹᵻtˈɜːnz ðə sˈɜːvɪs, ɔːlɹˌɛdi wˈaɪɚd tʊ ɪts ɹᵻpˈɑːzɪtˌɔːɹi.

scenes.text: The context also publishes events. Close it, and managed cleanup runs.
scenes.phonemes: ðə kˈɑːntɛkst ˈɔːlsoʊ pˈʌblɪʃᵻz ᵻvˈɛnts. klˈoʊs ɪt, ænd mˈænɪdʒd klˈiːnʌp ɹˈʌnz.

scenes.text: Our tests confirm: same service, one event, cleanup called. Definitions describe; instances do the work.
scenes.phonemes: ˌaʊɚ tˈɛsts kənfˈɜːm: sˈeɪm sˈɜːvɪs, wˈʌn ᵻvˈɛnt, klˈiːnʌp kˈɔːld. dˌɛfɪnˈɪʃənz dᵻskɹˈaɪb; ˈɪnstənsᵻz dˈuː ðə wˈɜːk.
